name: Lewisham

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers most of the borough (three designations, from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2029) for privately rented homes not covered by HMO licensing; Telegraph Hill and parts of Blackheath are not included.
licensing.additional: Additional HMO licensing covers the whole borough for HMOs let to three or four unrelated people (larger ones need a mandatory licence), from 5 April 2022 until 4 April 2027.
licensing.fee: A selective licence costs £640 for five years: £160 on application and £480 when it is granted, with discounts for accredited landlords and charities taken off the second payment.

housing: Lewisham has a mix of Victorian terraces and villas, many converted into flats, inter-war cottage estates in Bellingham and Downham, and post-war council blocks in Deptford and New Cross. Social renting is high and more than a quarter of households rented privately at the 2021 Census. Goldsmiths keeps a student market in New Cross, while new towers in Lewisham town centre and along the Deptford riverside have added many rented flats.
checkinTips: Victorian conversions in Brockley and Forest Hill: photograph sash windows, cornices, fireplaces and any cracks in the ceilings.
Student shared houses in New Cross: photograph each bedroom lock and furniture, the shared kitchen and the fire alarm and fire doors.
Ex-council houses in Bellingham and Downham: photograph the garden, fences, sheds and outside drains, and check windows and doors close properly.
New-build flats in Lewisham and Deptford: record fobs, bike store and bin store access, and photograph the ventilation unit and balcony.
Flats on hillside streets: photograph steps, paths and boundary walls, and look for damp on walls built against the slope.
tenantHelp: Lewisham Council's private sector housing team can inspect privately rented homes for disrepair and hazards; contact it through lewisham.gov.uk.
